Priya M.: Thanks for a great all-hands. Quick follow-up: teams want a single-page reference for the release cadence/oncall/SLA decisions. Can we capture the decisions and owners here?
Sam H.: TL;DR we want predictable windows, not one-size-fits-all. Prefer 3-week planning as the default to reduce mid-sprint churn, but teams may keep 2 or 4 weeks if they document trade-offs in their team page.
Mei Z.: Will the oncall model change with cadence?
Sam H.: Yes 1 primary oncall will move to 7-day rotations (Mon-Sun) to reduce weekday handoffs; secondaries and escalation ladders remain. The idea is fewer handovers per sprint boundary.
Jules K.: Are we introducing any release freezes for major infra changes?
Sam H.: Not blanket freezes. For infra-impacting changes we will use scheduled maintenance windows and explicit blackout periods communicated one week ahead. Teams must add the maintenance tag in deployments.
Aria L.: Paging/SLA specifics? Any tightened ack windows?
Sam H.: Paging rules unchanged: sev1 pages immediate, ack <= 15m, mitigation plan <= 30m. We are clarifying runbook checkboxes so the 15/30 targets have concrete actions (who does what, and what a mitigation plan looks like).
Ken P.: Customer-facing SLA question: what are we committing for Dedicated? p95 or p99?
Sam H.: For Dedicated we publish both: p95 <= 250ms for standard gen profiles; p99 <= 1s as a stability guardrail. Long-context models will have per-profile SLAs (e.g., 64k context p95 <= 700ms, p99 <= 2s). Hosted will have slightly different published numbers (listed in the model catalog).
Mei Z.: How do rollouts get gated on quality?
Sam H.: New rule: every model rollout must include a prerelease eval harness (baseline prompts + acceptance metrics) and a canary with automated checks. Hard rollback thresholds: if error_rate increases by >0.5% or quality_regressions > 1% in canary, we rollback. Safety checks include toxicity/regeneration scans and embedding-similarity no-regression (configurable per model).
Jules K.: Can we get the default canary template to paste into deploys?
Sam H.: Default canary template (teams may tune per-model):
```json
{"rollout": {"canary_percent": 5, "stages": [5, 25, 100], "metrics": ["p95_latency","p99_latency","error_rate","quality_regressions"], "rollback_on": {"error_rate_delta_pct": 0.5, "quality_regressions_pct": 1.0}, "auto_promote_after": 2}}
```
Aria L.: CI auto-promote behavior?
Sam H.: CI will auto-promote after 2 consecutive green evaluations and no new errors for 30m. Ops can abort or force-rollback from the deployment dashboard.
Mei Z.: Who owns runbooks, post-release checks, and SLA comms?
Jules K.: I'll own runbook updates (PR to infra/runbooks).
Aria L.: I'll own the post-release checklist and publish the eval prompt sets.
Ken P.: I'll draft customer-facing SLA language and update the status page + notify account teams.
Priya M.: Action items recap: Sam to add canary template to infra deploy repo; Jules to refresh runbooks; Aria to publish eval harness and checklists; Ken to prepare SLA comms. Drop PR/links in #eng-process and ping leadership when ready. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: deployment queued for release/infra-2026-07 at 2187654444 :rocket:
Mei Z.: Any change to postmortem timing?
Sam H.: Keeping the blameless timing but tightening initial summary: initial incident summary within 48h, full RCA within 7 days. We'll add automated 30m and 24h post-deploy health checks for major rollouts to surface regressions quickly.
Priya M.: Great 1 let's keep this thread for short status updates only. Leadership will review progress in the next ops sync.
Jules K.: PR for runbook updates incoming today.
Aria L.: Eval harness will be published by EOD tomorrow.
Ken P.: SLA draft to reviewers in a few hours.
Priya M.: Thanks everyone. :white_check_mark:
